title: Normalization and other Data Modeling Methods
summary: Introduces functional dependency, modification anomalies, progressive normal forms, and the relationship between normalization and other design methods.

concepts.title: Functional dependency
concepts.summary: A functional dependency exists when one attribute set determines the value of another and provides the basis for normalization decisions.

concepts.title: Modification anomalies
concepts.summary: Poorly structured relations can make insert, update, or delete operations lose facts or require inconsistent repetition.

concepts.title: First normal form
concepts.summary: A first-normal-form relation has single-valued columns; repeating or multivalued facts are represented in related rows instead.

concepts.title: Second normal form
concepts.summary: A relation in second normal form is in first normal form and has no nonkey attribute that depends on only part of a composite key.

concepts.title: Third normal form
concepts.summary: A third-normal-form design removes nonkey facts that depend on other nonkey facts rather than directly on the key.

concepts.title: Boyce-Codd normal form
concepts.summary: BCNF strengthens dependency rules by requiring every determinant to be a candidate key.

concepts.title: Higher normal forms
concepts.summary: Later normal forms address multivalued, join, and domain-key dependencies that are not resolved by the first three forms.

concepts.title: Alternative design methods
concepts.summary: Normalization and conceptual data modeling use different procedures but should converge on structures that faithfully represent the same facts.
